authored_from: Articles (Serious)/technical/3B1B — Editing - Formal Execution.md, §III (the migration predicate), §IV (the safe-change asymmetry) and §VIII (Expand–Migrate–Contract)
note: SPEC vectors for the migration function μ and the Expand–Migrate–Contract sequence. Authored from the article, not generated from the reference engine.

divergence.statement: This is the last piece of M-EDIT, and the reference engine has none of it.

term_by_term.μ has a representation: RUST-AHEAD. The reference has no migration function at all. Its classification is binary — compatible, or refused — because 'migratable' needs a μ to represent it with. Its own discipline is REFUSE-IF-UNSAFE, never migrate: check_definition_edit_safety returns {'status': 'refused', 'blocked_by': [...]} and stops there.
term_by_term.Safe(e, μ) judges μ(sᵢ): RUST-AHEAD, and it is the difference that matters. The reference evaluates candidate invariants against each instance's state AS IT STANDS. With a declared μ the check is on the MIGRATED state — which is what turns an edit that would be refused into one the instances are carried into.
term_by_term.Expand–Migrate–Contract: RUST-AHEAD. No transition period exists in the reference: an edit is one destructive step or it is refused. There is no D†, so there is no moment where both shapes coexist.
term_by_term.backward/forward compatibility: RUST-AHEAD. Neither direction is named or computed anywhere in the reference, so 'this commits you' cannot be surfaced at author time because there is nothing that knows it.

divergence.what_python_does_have_and_why_it_is_not_: The reference's refuse-if-unsafe IS a real safety property and is at parity in shape with Safe(e, id) — recorded as such in editing.json. What it lacks is the escape: it can say NO, and it cannot offer a way through. That is the whole of EDIT-12.
divergence.when_python_catches_up: These cases become parity vectors unchanged; nothing in them is Rust-specific.
divergence.not_a_divergence_in: R1 behaviour. Migration is a new additive module; Migration::Identity remains the default and every prior vector runs unchanged under it.

mu_cases.name: mu_moves_a_value_into_the_new_shape
mu_cases.why: μ at last has a representation. The copy leaves the old shape in place, which is what makes the transition period safe.

mu_cases.name: mu_backfills_a_default
mu_cases.why: A new dimension needs a value in every live instance, and the declared default is where it comes from.

mu_cases.name: a_missing_source_is_an_error_not_a_silent_skip
mu_cases.why: Quietly doing nothing for an instance that does not have what the migration assumed is exactly how a half-migrated estate happens — and nobody notices until something reads it.

safe_cases.name: safe_now_judges_the_migrated_state_not_the_original
safe_cases.why: THE point of EDIT-12, in one case. The same edit against the same instances: refused under μ = id, admitted under a declared μ. Refuse-if-unsafe becomes migrate.

safe_cases.name: a_mu_that_does_not_deliver_is_still_refused
safe_cases.why: μ is an escape from refusal, not an exemption from the check. A migration that leaves an instance outside V_D' is reported exactly as before.

asymmetry_cases.name: only_three_kinds_can_strand
asymmetry_cases.why: §IV's asymmetry, made exact: `Safe` evaluates the candidate's invariants against live states, so an edit strands only if it ADDS or TIGHTENS an invariant, or changes what a value means. This is what makes e₊ AUTO-SAFE WITH NO CHECK rather than merely cheap.

asymmetry_cases.name: expand_must_be_a_weakening
asymmetry_cases.why: Expand–Migrate–Contract only works if the new shape is added BESIDE the old, never instead of it. An e₊ that could strand is refused at plan time, before anything runs.

sequence_cases.name: the_three_phases_run_in_order_and_every_instance_arrives
sequence_cases.why: D --e₊--> D† --μ--> D† --e₋--> D'. One call, because the ordering IS the safety property.

sequence_cases.name: the_transition_period_is_recorded_not_collapsed
sequence_cases.why: D† is a real version node with BOTH shapes present, so the transition period is inspectable rather than a moment nobody can see. The destructive step is sequenced last, and only then is the old shape gone.

sequence_cases.name: at_no_point_is_an_instance_without_a_shape_that_holds_it
sequence_cases.why: The article's own summary of why the pattern exists. Checked at each step rather than inferred from the ordering: held by D before, held by D† during, still held by D† after μ.

sequence_cases.name: a_migration_that_does_not_deliver_is_refused_at_the_contract
sequence_cases.why: The article says Safe(e₋, id) holds BY CONSTRUCTION. That is a claim worth VERIFYING rather than trusting: if μ was wrong, saying so at the contract beats discovering it later.

compatibility_cases.name: a_migration_that_keeps_the_old_shape_is_both_ways
compatibility_cases.why: μ copies without erasing, so new code reads old data AND old code reads new data. Rollback stays open.

compatibility_cases.name: a_migration_that_erases_the_old_shape_is_one_way_and_says_so_up_front
compatibility_cases.why: Forward compatibility is required BECAUSE ROLLBACK EXISTS — D's Enzymes must survive states μ already touched. An edit that achieves only backward compatibility may still be the right edit, but 'this commits you' is a fact the author is entitled to AT AUTHOR TIME, not a discovery made during a rollback. Available from `plan`, before `run` is ever called.

knock_on_cases.name: journalling_the_pre_image_collapses_partial_rollback_to_total
knock_on_cases.why: The link to EDIT-7. A bare RetireDim of a genesis dimension rolls back Partial — nothing recorded what was lost. Run through Expand–Migrate–Contract, μ journals what it erased, so μ⁻¹ becomes a lookup and the same rollback is Total. A lossy migration made losslessly reversible at the storage cost the article names.

knock_on_cases.name: the_pre_image_carries_the_real_erased_value
knock_on_cases.why: A lookup, not an inference — the actual value the instance held, not a reconstruction.
